RECOMMENDATION: IT DEPENDS
LIKELIHOOD: 45

The all-male panel is not evidence on its own. Panels often reflect who currently holds senior posts, and all-male bodies appoint women regularly. As a standalone claim it looks weak and invites dismissal.

Your strong point is the qualifications comparison: a master's in educational leadership plus five years actually doing deputy-principal work against "courses" and classroom years. That is concrete and checkable. The unanswered request is also significant — in many jurisdictions an employer must give written reasons on request, and silence shifts pressure onto them.

So: lead with qualifications and the missing explanation. Mention panel composition only as background context, if at all. Send a written follow-up with a deadline before deciding anything further.
